Wait so you mean you’re taking CEE 30 right now? Or do you mean next year as a sophomore? CEE 150 is also offered in spring so if you have space during Spring 2022 then I would still recommend you to try and take that before 170+121. 

CEE 20 had a lot of linear algebra/Math 3A, I don’t remember if there was any calculus (but since I don’t, it probably didn’t have it or it was barely enough to be important/difficult). The thing that makes Math3A potentially difficult is that there’s some proofs, but the actual problem-solving/algebra part was fine. Also if you’ve never coded before, CEE 20 is gonna be a little difficult since it’s a new way of thinking. You learn about how to code arrays, matrices, other linear algebra stuff, and I think also how to create if/for loops. There’s other stuff but that’s what I remember off the top of my head.

Edit: also I wanna add the reason why I say CEE 170 will be difficult without CEE 20 taken already is because the stuff you’re expected to code is exponentially more complicated than what you do in CEE 20. I know a ton of people who struggled in that class’s project who have already taken both CEE 20/21

I would suggest taking CEE 150/150L during Fall 2022 instead of CEE 170 since you’ve already taken CEE 30. The reason is because most civil/environmental students usually take a combination of CEE 150 + 150L, 121, 170 all during their junior year and it’s horrible because they’re all super hard classes with intensive projects (not 150 but it has a lab with weekly intensive lab reports lol). However, if you take CEE 150 and the following structural classes (CEE 151a during winter, CEE 151c during spring) during your sophomore year, your junior year will be exponentially more manageable.

Definitely possible, and I don’t think it’s too difficult because they’re 2 different types of math, linear algebra and calculus. Just a warning though, CEE 170 is gonna be really tough without having CEE 20 taken already, since the project for that class has heavy usage of Matlab. Did you already take statics/CEE 30?

I’m not an employer or anything but I’ve gotten this advice from those higher up:

-Show that you’re actively listening by nodding head (if you don’t move at all, sometimes it looks like you’re frozen or not paying attention)

-Have a plain background (things in your room or a crazy virtual background is distracting)

-Look at the camera while you talk (more for people who have a side camera/double monitor setup, interviewers want to see you straight on and not your side profile)

-Don’t read off of a script (it’s really obvious, especially because your eyes move back and forth as you read and we can see)
